name: plainsong-mcp

tools.name: analyze_features
tools.description: Describe a piece as sixteen numbers per bar -- density, register, tension, syncopation, dynamics and the rest -- so a model can perceive what is written.

content.description: Notation to analyse instead of a path.

session.description: An ensemble session to analyse instead.

voice.description: One voice by name. Default is the whole texture.

table.description: Also return a fixed-width table for reading.

tools.name: apply_directives
tools.description: Apply a bandleader's directive JSON to a piece or an ensemble session and return the result as data: the directives as they were read, what the arrangement was before and after, and the sixteen features per bar of each. Use conduct_score instead when you want the timing report in prose.

directives.description: The directive JSON. Call directive_reference for the shape.

frame.description: Whose ears: conductor, audience, player:<name>, score.

features.description: Include the feature vectors. On by default.

tools.name: compile_score
tools.description: Compile notation to MIDI and audio, returning the arrangement summary and any diagnostics. Pass either a path or inline content.

content.description: Notation to compile instead of a path.

audio.description: Also render audio. Slower; off by default.

tools.name: conduct_score
tools.description: Apply a bandleader's directive JSON to a piece and report what it did to the ensemble's timing: how the arrivals moved together and how far each player's hands moved to keep them there.

content.description: Notation to conduct instead of a path.

frame.description: Whose ears: conductor, audience, player:<name>, or score.

tools.name: directive_reference
tools.description: Read the conductor's directive vocabulary -- the JSON a bandleader sends, which actions the timing layer acts on, and what the windows and targets mean. Call this before writing directives for the first time in a session.

tools.name: ensemble_join
tools.description: Claim one voice of a session. A voice has one owner at a time, so claiming is how agents avoid choosing the same part. Returns everything needed to start writing.

voice.description: Voice to claim: @bass, @violin1, chords, melody, lyrics.

takeover.description: Take a held voice. Only when its owner has stopped.

tools.name: ensemble_leave
tools.description: Release a voice you hold so another agent can take it.

tools.name: ensemble_log
tools.description: Read the session's change log, oldest first. This is how a joining agent finds out what has already happened.

tools.name: ensemble_open
tools.description: Open a shared session several agents can write to, or reopen one that exists. Sets the key, tempo, metre and form every part is written against.

sections.description: The form: names, or objects with name, description and bars.

voices.description: Voices to advertise: @bass, @violin1, chords, melody, lyrics.

tools.name: ensemble_read
tools.description: Read a session in one call: key, tempo, metre, form, which voices exist and who holds them, what every voice plays in the bars you are about to write, your own part, the version to write against, and what has changed recently.

session.description: Session name. Omit to list the sessions.

voice.description: Your voice, to get its content and version.

bars.description: Bars to look at, such as '5-8'. Default is all of them.

history.description: How many log entries to include (default 8).

tools.name: ensemble_render
tools.description: Merge the parts and compile the session to MIDI, and optionally audio.

audio.description: Also render audio. Slower; off by default.

tools.name: ensemble_report
tools.description: Report what a listener on the stage actually hears: each voice's distance, speech time, propagation delay and the moment its player has to act, plus the spread at the chosen listener and at every other one.

content.description: Notation to analyse instead of a path.

frame.description: Whose ears: conductor, audience, player:<name>, or score.

tools.name: ensemble_status
tools.description: The short view of a session: version, voices, who holds what, bar count and whether the merged score still compiles. Omit the name to list sessions.

session.description: Session name. Omit to list the sessions.

tools.name: ensemble_write_part
tools.description: Write your voice's part. The notation is parsed and checked against the session header before anything reaches disk. Pass the base_version you read; if the voice has moved on the write is refused and you are given the current part to rebase onto.

content.description: The part: section headers and rows for your voice only, no header block.

base_version.description: The version you read this voice at.

summary.description: One line saying what you changed, for the log.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List files in the working directory.

path.description: Directory relative to the working directory. Defaults to the root.

tools.name: notation_reference
tools.description: Read the Plainsong notation reference. Call this before writing notation for the first time in a session.

tools.name: probe_host
tools.description: Report what this machine can do: platform, optional libraries, soundfonts, MIDI ports, audio playback, network. Use it before choosing how to render or connect.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file from the working directory or the project.

tools.name: read_library
tools.description: Read one file from the bundled notation library, by name or title.

tools.name: record_decision
tools.description: Append a line to the build journal, recording a decision and why it was made.

note.description: What was decided and the reason.

tools.name: search_library
tools.description: Search the bundled notation library for reference material by title, key or style.

tools.name: speech_profiles
tools.description: List the instrument speech profiles a [Stage] block can name, with how long each takes to sound and how far into the attack the ear places it.

tools.name: stage_reference
tools.description: Read how to write a [Stage] block: positions, listeners, speech profiles and feel. Call this before writing arrival-centric timing for the first time in a session.

tools.name: transpose_score
tools.description: Transpose a notation file to another key, writing the result next to it.

tools.name: verify_specs
tools.description: Run the project's specs and report what passes and what fails. Use this after making a change to check whether it worked.

tag.description: Only run specs carrying this tag.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write a text file into the working directory, creating parent directories.

path.description: Path to write, relative to the working directory.

tools.name: write_score
tools.description: Write Plainsong notation to a .song file. The notation is parsed first and the result reports any problems, so use this rather than write_file for music.

instructions:
Plainsong compiles plain-text music notation to MIDI and audio.

Read plainsong://notation-reference before writing notation for the first time.
Write music with write_score or ensemble_write_part rather than write_file: both
parse the notation before anything reaches disk.

Several agents can write one score at once. Open or read a session with
ensemble_read, claim one voice with ensemble_join, and write only that voice.
Every write carries the version you read it at, so a part that moved under you
is refused rather than overwritten.
